name: Tramping Paws
summary: At Greenwarden's Grove in the Wetlands, Rethiel watches the Mosshide numbers rise near the Gate of Algaz. Their fires and trampling threaten the bog, and Rethiel asks travelers to thin their ranks.

sections.title: A Swelling Fen Menace
sections.body: Mosshide gnolls lived in the Wetlands for many years without overwhelming the natural order. Now their numbers have surged south toward the pass of Dun Algaz. Their heavy boots and paws crush rare fen plants, while their logging strips groves for campsite fires. If the packs keep growing, the fragile marsh will suffer.

sections.title: The Greenwarden's Judgment
sections.body: Rethiel the Greenwarden watches the marsh for signs of imbalance. The gnolls' existence is not the trouble; their numbers have grown beyond what the Wetlands can support. Thinning the Mosshide gnolls and mongrels helps preserve the fen, and may earn the approval of its ancient guardian.

faq.answer: Rethiel is a bog beast who lives in the Wetlands along the road between Ironforge's borders and Arathi. Dedicated to preserving the marsh, Rethiel watches the land's health and asks travelers to keep destructive populations in check.

faq.q: Why are the Mosshide gnolls a problem now?
faq.answer: The Mosshide gnolls once lived alongside the marsh without lasting harm, but their recent population boom has brought heavy logging for firewood and widespread trampling of fragile marsh plants.

faq.q: Where are the gnolls causing this damage?
faq.answer: Mosshide gnolls and mongrels gather in large numbers in the southern Wetlands, especially near the dwarven pass of Dun Algaz.

faq.q: What comes after culling the gnolls?
faq.answer: After the packs are thinned, Rethiel investigates the cause of their unusual activity and fuel use, then sends travelers to Fire Taboo.

faq.q: Why does Rethiel mention having its faith tested?
faq.answer: Rethiel says its faith in your people has been taxed in the past, and it remains wary of mortals and their rapid expansion. Helping protect the wild fen shows that mortals can care for nature rather than exploit it.

angles.text: As a druid, you share the Cenarion duty to keep nature in balance. Thinning an unnatural population surge can help keep the marsh from collapsing.
As a night elf, you share old bonds with nature's wild spirits. Helping Rethiel heal the marsh is a familiar and honored duty.
As a dwarf, you know the gnolls swarm just outside the Gate of Algaz. Thinning their ranks protects the fen and secures the vital road between Ironforge and Menethil Harbor.
